result.description: Application monitoring and error tracking platform that surfaces errors, performance issues and traces for developers.
result.auth_detail: Bearer auth tokens (organization tokens via internal integration, personal user tokens with scopes); OAuth2 authorization code grant for third-party apps (access tokens expire after 30 days, refresh tokens). Legacy API keys disabled for new accounts.
result.access_detail: Anyone can sign up at sentry.io, create an internal integration or personal token in the UI, and call the API. A free Developer plan exists; the pricing page feature table has an API row that may differ by plan, so the free-tier API limit is not fully confirmed. Public OAuth apps are created from organization settings.
result.api_notes: REST web API covering organizations, projects, issues, events, releases, teams, members, alerts, replays, monitors and more. Full OpenAPI reference at docs.sentry.io/api.

evidence.quote: Connects AI assistants to Sentry for searching errors, analyzing performance, triaging issues, reading documentation, and managing projects — all via the Model Context Protocol.
For third-party applications that need to access Sentry on behalf of users, Sentry supports OAuth2 with the authorization code grant type.
These auth tokens can be created within Sentry on the "User settings" page (User settings > Personal Tokens) and assigned specific scopes.
You can create authentication tokens within Sentry by creating an internal integration.
To use Sentry's APIs, you must have an authentication token.
The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically.
The base MCP server address is: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`
API keys are a legacy means of authenticating. They will still be supported but are disabled for new accounts.
